oracle.name: IRS Publication 15-T (2026) wage-bracket and percentage-method tables and worksheets (federal); state worked examples per jurisdiction annex
oracle.notes: Federal oracle answered (US-MQ-08, 2026-10-29): Pub. 15-T 2026 has no full percentage-method worked example; Stage 9b re-derives from Worksheet 1A + Annual Percentage Method tables and uses the two published examples (NRA 526.90 -> 31; tribal 6,000 -> 584.09) [US-FED-027]. in_scope.channel: outbound via the third-party filing provider hand-off (no ADP integration; owner, biweekly 2026-10-21)
in_scope.note: To every State where withholding applies; States without a wage income tax are stated in annex section 2. IN county, MD county (MW506) and NYC/Yonkers (NYS-45/NYS-1) are piggy-backed on the State withholding return (T3), not separate locality returns [US-INS5-007, US-MDP51-001, US-NY-008]. Combined State returns carry other items on the same return: OR Form OQ (withholding, UI, Paid Leave, Workers' Benefit Fund, TriMet and Lane transit, statewide transit tax) [US-ORS5-010]; NY NYS-45 (withholding, wage reporting, UI) [US-NYS5-010]; NJ NJ-927 / WR-30 (income tax, UI, TDI, FLI) [US-NJP51-001, US-NJS5-017]; NM TRD-41431 (workers' compensation fee and quarterly wage and withholding report) [US-NMS5-012]; VT WHT-436 (Child Care Contribution) [US-VTS5-030].

in_scope.filing_id: State unemployment insurance quarterly contribution and wage report (per State)

in_scope.channel: outbound via the third-party filing provider hand-off (no ADP integration; owner, biweekly 2026-10-21)
in_scope.ccg_location: CCG m10 Table 10.1.2; each annex section 5
in_scope.note: Filed to the State of UI coverage only (localization test). The UI return carries the State UI-linked administrative / workforce / solvency levies (US-OWN-007, second limb), except where a levy is billed separately (WV annual fee, billed by WorkForce WV, not on the quarterly UI return [US-WVS5-002]). RI TX-17 is one report for UI, TDI and JDA [US-RIS5-017]; WY UI and workers' compensation are reported jointly [US-WYS5-007]; event-driven UI reports such as the SC UCB-113 mass-separation report [US-SCS5-007] and the GA mass-separation report [US-GAS5-020] are part of this obligation. US-GAS5-020 is a partial register row (GDOL proposed rule; adopted text not read).

in_scope.filing_id: State PFML / SDI / LTC programme reports where separate from the State wage return (per State)
in_scope.channel: outbound via the third-party filing provider hand-off (no ADP integration; owner, biweekly 2026-10-21)
in_scope.ccg_location: CCG m05; annexes WA, CT, CO, DE, ME, MD, MN, MA, DC section 3/5
in_scope.note: Premium State follows the UI localization test unless a State rule differs (routing, CCG Annex MULTI) [US-MULTIS5-024]. Separate programme reports per the MANDATE sdi_tdi_pfml census: WA Paid Leave + WA Cares (one combined report) [US-WAPFML-001, US-WALTC-001, US-WAB5-003], CT Paid Leave (file specification toolkit US-CTB5-001) [US-CTS5-022], CO FAMLI [US-COS5-008], DE Paid Leave [US-DES5-013], ME PFML [US-MES5-024], MD FAMLI from 2027-01-01 (no contribution in 2026) [US-MDS5-014]. Annex section 5 adds MN Paid Leave (quarterly wage detail and premium to DEED) [US-MNS5-018], MA PFML (contribution to DFML; return channel and mechanics are an open non-blocking item of the MA annex) [US-MAS5-012] and DC Paid Family Leave (employer-only, quarterly via ESSP) [US-DCS5-019]. Not separate: CA SDI is filed on the DE 9 / DE 9C State wage return [US-CAP7-002] and OR Paid Leave on Form OQ [US-OR-002] (T3, filed with the State wage return); NJ TDI / FLI go on NJ-927 / WR-30 [US-NJS5-017]; RI TDI goes on the TX-17 UI report [US-RIS5-017]; NY DBL / PFL and HI TDI are insurer-funded with no State report (data-problem) [US-NYB5-401, US-NYB5-402, US-HI-003]. VT has no mandatory SDI / PFML programme [US-VTP51-006]; the VT Child Care Contribution is reported on WHT-436, the withholding return [US-VTS5-030]. VA paid family and medical leave contributions start 2028-04-01 [US-VAS5-016], so there is no VA programme report for 2026.

tier.verdict_verbatim: Overall T4 (discriminator confirmed 2026-10-29 on source-read evidence; per-jurisdiction census completed at seal attempt 3 and re-checked at seal attempts 4, 5 and 6, 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-02; mandate sealed 2026-11-02 with all 65 questions answered; the limbs reopened and closed at seal attempt 6 (US-MQ-26 CT, US-MQ-45 MS, US-MQ-57 OR) bear on no tier; Stage-5 re-check 2026-11-02: superseded citations re-pointed to their S5 successors, census unchanged (new local layers found only inside T4 states: Lexington KY, Greenwood Village and Glendale CO OPT), and the five prevailing-wage limbs reopened that day (US-MQ-30 GA, 32 IA, 45 MS, 47 NC, 64 UT) and closed at the reseal the same day bear on no tier). Employer-operation test: T4 requires a second independent calculation AND a separate remittance/return to a second authority. Federal: 26 U.S.C. 3402(a)(1) obliges every employer to withhold federal income tax under IRS tables and covers federal tax only [US-FED-012]; FICA and FUTA go on federal returns 941/944/940 [US-FED-005, US-FED-007, US-FED-015]. State: a wage-taxing state imposes its own withholding computed on its own basis (e.g. Va. Code 58.1-461 [US-VAPIT-002]) remitted to the state revenue authority on its own returns (Virginia Tax VA-5/VA-6 [US-VAPIT-003]); state UI is a separate state tax base and agency (Fla. Stat. 443.1216 [US-MULTI-001]; SC Code ch. 41-31 [US-SCS5-015]). Nothing is absorbed into the federal deduction (contrast Switzerland, StHG Art. 36a Abs. 1, where one deduction discharges all levels). FUTA is federal but its credit depends on state UI paid and on the state's Title XII loan status (26 U.S.C. 3302(c)(2) [US-FED-014]): a cross-layer dependency, so futa is T3. Inside a state, a local layer is T4 where a locality receives a separate return (City of Portland Metro SHS / Multnomah PFA [US-ORS5-004]; Ohio municipal income tax, ORC 718.03 [US-OHP52-003]; Pennsylvania Act 32 EIT/LST to the local collector [US-PA-004]; Jersey City and Newark employer payroll taxes on quarterly city returns [US-NJP6-001, US-NJP6-002]) and T3 where it is piggybacked on the state return (Maryland county tax on MW506 [US-MDP51-001]; NYC and Yonkers on NYS-45/NYS-1 [US-NY-008]). Consequence: the federal core and each jurisdiction are declared and scoped as parallel layers, and the multistate domain routes each employee to one or more of them. Jurisdiction annexes (re-checked 2026-10-30, seal attempt 5): 9 T1 (no state wage tax; SUI and levies only: AK, FL, NH, NV, SD, TN, TX, WA, WY; WA declares the Seattle payroll expense tax, a threshold-conditional employer tax on a city return [US-WAP51-001], as a T4-shaped element), 31 T3 (state withholding, local layer absent or piggybacked on the state return), 11 T4 (local layer remitted to the locality on its own return: AL occupational taxes [US-ALP51-001], CO Denver OPT [US-COP52-001], DE Wilmington [US-DEP52-001], KY occupational taxes [US-KYP52-002], MI 23 self-administering cities [US-MIP52-002], MO St. Louis/Kansas City [US-MOP52-006], NJ Jersey City/Newark employer payroll taxes filed with the city [US-NJP6-001, US-NJP6-002], OH [US-OHP52-003], OR [US-ORS5-004], PA [US-PA-004], WV municipal service fees withheld and remitted to the city, W. Va. Code 8-13-13 [US-WVR3-001], Charleston [US-WVR3-002]); 0 unclassified; no classification rests on MANUAL/gated evidence.
